title: Root-distribution conjecture for Kadar–Yu Chebyshev polynomials
statement:
Fix an integer $l$ and let $\lambda\vdash l+2$. For each $k\geq -1$, let $P^{(\lambda)}_{l+4+k}(\alpha)$ be the associated polynomial.

**Root-distribution conjecture.** For each $k\geq -1$, the polynomial $P^{(\lambda)}_{l+4+k}$ is square free. Furthermore, for sufficiently large $k$, it has a fixed number of roots outside $[-2,2]$, and

$$
\bigcup_{k=0}^{\infty}\{\alpha\in[-2,2]\mid P^{(\lambda)}_{l+4+k}(\alpha)=0\}
$$

is dense in $[-2,2]$.

The claim summarizes the root patterns observed for several partition families. It predicts both eventual stability of the number of exterior roots and density of the interior roots.
references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2015–2025). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1601.04382](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.04382), [arXiv:1510.01758](https://arxiv.org/abs/1510.01758).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24535

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).
source_name: Benjamin Morris and Paul P. Martin, “On semisimplicity criteria and non-semisimple representation theory for the Kadar-Yu algebras”, arXiv:2512.24535 (2025).
